info.title: ReconAgent API
info.description: ReconAgent backend — AI finance controller over a normalized internal financial data model (synthetic dataset for deterministic demos and evaluation).

get.description: Computes gross/successful/failed/refunded/net/settlement amounts (exact minor-unit integers) grouped by currency over the filtered window. Dates are inclusive UTC calendar days; `status`/`method` filter payments, `currency` applies to all resources.

get.summary: List stored payments with finance filters
get.description: Returns one bounded page of stored payments (exact minor-unit amounts) filtered by an inclusive UTC date window, currency, payment status, and method.

get.summary: List stored refunds with finance filters
get.description: Returns one bounded page of stored refunds filtered by an inclusive UTC date window, currency, refund status, or parent payment id.

get.summary: List stored settlements with finance filters
get.description: Returns one bounded page of stored settlements (amount/fees/tax in exact minor units) filtered by an inclusive UTC date window, currency, and settlement status.

get.summary: List stored orders with finance filters
get.description: Returns one bounded page of stored orders filtered by an inclusive UTC date window, currency, order status, and receipt.

get.summary: Deterministic payment performance metrics for a named period
get.description: Transaction volume, successful/failed/in-progress counts and success/failure rates over a named reporting period resolved in IST (specification Part 2). Rates use transaction volume as denominator and are null when the period is empty. No LLM, no estimates — pure aggregation over stored payments.

parameters.name: period

schema.description: Named reporting period: today, yesterday, this_week, previous_week, this_month, previous_month (IST calendar semantics)
schema.title: Period

parameters.description: Named reporting period: today, yesterday, this_week, previous_week, this_month, previous_month (IST calendar semantics)

get.summary: Deterministic revenue metrics for a named period
get.description: Gross revenue (captured payments incl. refunded-status ones), processed-only refund amount/count/rate, Razorpay fee/tax sums, and the three separately-labeled net-revenue variants over a named reporting period resolved in IST (specification Parts 3-4).

parameters.name: period

schema.description: Named reporting period: today, yesterday, this_week, previous_week, this_month, previous_month (IST calendar semantics)
schema.title: Period

parameters.description: Named reporting period: today, yesterday, this_week, previous_week, this_month, previous_month (IST calendar semantics)

get.summary: Period-over-period trend for one finance metric
get.description: Compares a supported metric (transaction_volume, successful_transactions, failed_transactions, gross_revenue, razorpay_fee, razorpay_tax, refund_amount, refund_count, settlement_amount, settlement_fees, settlement_tax) across current vs previous day/week/month windows resolved in IST. Returns both values, absolute change, percentage change, and an explicit changeType; percentage change is null with 'new_activity'/'no_activity' when the previous value is zero (specification Part 6.4).

post.summary: Ask a finance question in natural language
post.description: Plans read-only Finance Tool calls for the question, executes them against synced records, derives deterministic financial signals, and returns an LLM-written explanation grounded in those signals. `tool_results` / `financial_signals` carry the exact numbers; `answer` is interpretation only.

post.summary: Stream AI finance chat response as Server-Sent Events
post.description: SSE variant of /chat. Streams token events as they arrive from the LLM, followed by a complete event with the full response.

post.summary: Run deterministic batch reconciliation over a synthetic dataset
post.description: Executes the reconcile_transactions Finance Tool — fixed matching rules over a seeded 50+ case synthetic batch — and returns the summary metrics, match rate, throughput, and the full exception list. With `explain=true` an LLM narrative is attached; it can only describe the returned numbers. `accuracy` is null at runtime by design: measured accuracy lives in the evaluation harness (scripts/reconcile_benchmark.py), never in serving.

get.summary: Evaluation-only: measured accuracy vs isolated ground truth
get.description: BENCHMARK/EVALUATION SURFACE. Runs the same seeded synthetic batch through the deterministic engine and then the isolated ground-truth evaluator, exposing measured accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and FP/FN. The serving endpoint (POST /reconcile) never sees ground truth and reports accuracy=null; only this explicitly-marked evaluation surface measures quality. Aggregate metrics and mismatch case ids are returned — never raw ground-truth records. No database, no LLM, no credentials.

post.summary: Compare two reconciliation runs (What Changed / Drift Analysis)
post.description: Deterministically compares previous vs current reconciliation runs and computes match-rate change, exception-count change, exposure change, category drifts, priority distribution shifts, and major drivers. With `explain=true` an LLM narrative is attached describing the backend-computed facts.

interpretation failed), ``failed`` (nothing could be retrieved).

AiReconcileRequest.title: AiReconcileRequest
AiReconcileRequest.description:
Request for one deterministic reconciliation run.

Mirrors :class:`~app.ai.tools.reconciliation.ReconcileToolInput` so
the HTTP boundary validates the exact same constraints the tool
enforces. Only dataset selection is accepted — never record contents
(unknown fields are rejected, not silently ignored).

AiReconcileResponse.title: AiReconcileResponse
AiReconcileResponse.description:
Deterministic reconciliation outcome plus optional LLM narrative.

``accuracy`` is ``None`` at runtime by design: ground truth exists
only inside the evaluation harness (generator/tests/benchmark), never
in the serving path — reporting a fabricated accuracy would defeat
its purpose. Run ``scripts/reconcile_benchmark.py`` for measured
accuracy against ground truth.

MetricRate.title: MetricRate
MetricRate.description:
A percentage that may be mathematically undefined.

Spec Part 6.4: a zero denominator yields ``value=None`` — never 0, never
an exception. ``basis`` labels exactly what was divided by what so the
definition travels with the number.

ReconciliationEvaluationReport.title: ReconciliationEvaluationReport
ReconciliationEvaluationReport.description:
MEASURED quality of one reconciliation run vs ground truth.

EVALUATION/BENCHMARK ONLY — this model exists solely for the
evaluation harness and ``GET /api/v1/ai/reconcile/evaluation``.
The serving endpoint (``POST /api/v1/ai/reconcile``) never touches
ground truth and reports ``accuracy=null``; here accuracy, precision,
recall and F1 are measured against the generator's isolated
expectations. Only aggregate metrics and mismatch case ids are
exposed — never raw ground-truth records.

ReconciliationEvidence.title: ReconciliationEvidence
ReconciliationEvidence.description:
Structured audit view of one deterministic decision.

Every field is **copied** from the records the engine already
reconciled (or from the decision itself) — nothing is recalculated
here and no new arithmetic exists in this vocabulary. The frontend
renders this payload verbatim to explain WHY a case was classified
the way it was; the LLM may narrate it but may never alter it.

``None`` means "not applicable to this case" (e.g. ``settlement_id``
on MISSING_SETTLEMENT), never an unknown value.

source_transaction_id.title: Source Transaction Id
source_transaction_id.description: Anchor record id: the payment id for payment-driven cases, the settlement line id when the payment side is missing, the refund id for orphaned refunds

matched_transaction_id.title: Matched Transaction Id
matched_transaction_id.description: Counterpart id used for the decision (None when absent)

difference_minor.title: Difference Minor
difference_minor.description: actual − expected in minor units; set on mismatches only

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Deterministic rule that decided the case

fee_minor.title: Fee Minor
fee_minor.description: Recorded provider fee included in math

tax_minor.title: Tax Minor
tax_minor.description: Recorded fee tax included in math

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Deterministic triage severity on the shared signal taxonomy (INFO/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL); None when the result was produced without triage annotation

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Documented bounded triage rank (CRITICAL=100, HIGH=80, MEDIUM=60, LOW=30, INFO=10); deterministic policy, not a learned risk score

recommended_action.title: Recommended Action
recommended_action.description: Deterministic operator guidance for exceptions; None for MATCHED (nothing to investigate)

financial_impact_minor.title: Financial Impact Minor
financial_impact_minor.description: Absolute financial exposure in minor units for this exception; None for MATCHED results or when impact cannot be safely determined from available evidence

financial_impact_reason.title: Financial Impact Reason
financial_impact_reason.description: Deterministic explanation of how financial_impact_minor was calculated; None when no impact is computed

evidence.description: Structured reconciliation evidence (payment/settlement/refund records, component amounts, expected vs actual, rules triggered, reason); None when not attached

ReconciliationResult.title: ReconciliationResult
ReconciliationResult.description:
One deterministic reconciliation decision.

``exception_type`` mirrors ``status`` for every non-matching outcome
and is ``None`` for ``MATCHED`` — consumers can filter exceptions
without knowing the status vocabulary.

Amount semantics: ``expected_amount_minor`` is the **expected
settlement** (gross minus available fee/tax/processed-refund
components), ``actual_amount_minor`` is what actually settled, and
the component fields expose exactly which deterministic inputs
produced that expectation so an LLM can explain the arithmetic
without recomputing it.

ReconciliationStatus.title: ReconciliationStatus
ReconciliationStatus.description:
Deterministic outcome of one reconciliation case.

Every value except ``MATCHED`` is an exception; ``UNRESOLVED`` marks
cases where no safe deterministic classification exists (the engine
refuses to guess rather than fabricating a verdict).

``AMOUNT_MISMATCH`` vs ``UNEXPLAINED_SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE``: the
former is a raw gross-vs-settled difference on a case with **no**
financial components available (legacy shape), the latter means the
engine subtracted the available fee/tax/refund components into an
expected settlement and the actual settlement still differed.

match_rate.title: Match Rate
match_rate.description: matched / total * 100 (2 decimals); None for an empty batch (spec Part 6.4 zero-denominator convention)

accuracy.title: Accuracy
accuracy.description: correct decisions / total * 100 vs ground truth; None without ground truth

ReconciliationSummary.title: ReconciliationSummary
ReconciliationSummary.description:
Batch-level deterministic metrics (no ground truth involved).

Rates are percentages rounded to two decimals purely for display;
``accuracy`` requires ground truth and is ``None`` when none was
supplied — never fabricated.

RefundEvidence.title: RefundEvidence
RefundEvidence.description:
One processed refund line inside :class:`ReconciliationEvidence`.

A verbatim copy of the refund record the engine debited — no derived
values, so the UI can itemize refunds without recomputing anything.

refund_rate.description: §4.3 definition A: refund amount / gross revenue × 100

RefundMetricsBlock.title: RefundMetricsBlock
RefundMetricsBlock.description: Refund metrics for one period (specification Part 4).

ReportingPeriod.title: ReportingPeriod
ReportingPeriod.description: Explicit reporting window (specification Part 11 validation rule).

RevenueMetricsResponse.title: RevenueMetricsResponse
RevenueMetricsResponse.description:
GET /finance/revenue — specification Part 3 metrics.

Note: "Successful Revenue" is deliberately absent — spec §3.2 defines it
as identical to Gross Revenue and recommends exposing it once.

TrendResponse.title: TrendResponse
TrendResponse.description:
GET /finance/trends/{metric} — specification Part 6.

``absolute_change`` is always defined; ``percentage_change`` is None
with an explicit ``change_type`` whenever the previous value is zero
(spec Part 6.4).

TrendWindow.title: TrendWindow
TrendWindow.description: One side of a trend comparison: its window and the metric value.
